title: Throttle-aware latency-proportional autoscaler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine variant that scales capacity proportionally to observed latency SLO violation mass while remaining aware of request throttling signals. The goal is to reduce oscillation caused by capacity-induced throttles (rate limits/Burst curtailments) and prevent runaway scale that increases cost without improving tail latency. This ticket covers policy design, simulator, implementation hooks in the scaling controller, and telemetry to validate behavior on Dedicated fleets.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler computes a single composite target based on: p95 latency gap, throttle_rate (requests/sec denied), and recent scale velocity; configurable weights must be exposed
When throttle_rate > configurable threshold, scale decisions incorporate throttle_dampening factor so new capacity growth is limited until throttles are resolved
Simulator demonstrates reduced scale oscillations compared to the baseline PID-like scaler on three canonical workloads (bursty chat, steady high-throughput, ramping traffic)
End-to-end integration test added: scaling decisions produce no more than 2x unnecessary capacity churn during synthetic 5x traffic spike test
Telemetry dashboards show the new metric 'throttle_aware_scale_factor' and policy-level tracing for rollouts
Documented rollout playbook and safe rollback steps exist in Confluence and the PRs link to them

decisions: Use latency gap at p95 as primary latency input; expose alternative percentiles via config
Throttle signal is computed from downstream 429/503 rate combined with internal rate-limiter rejects
Default damping curve: logistic with mid-point at throttle_rate = 0.5% of total requests, configurable
Policy defaults to conservative growth (max 20% additional capacity per decision) and allows burst overrides for critical tenants
tradeoffs: Conservative damping reduces cost and oscillation but may delay recovery after true capacity shortage
Including throttle signals prevents over-scaling when requests are being denied by per-tenant rate limits, but requires accurate throttle instrumentation
More aggressive defaults help latency at the expense of cost — default set to protect unit economics for non-enterprise tenants
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'throttle_aware_autoscaler' flag. Step 1: unit/integration tests and simulator validation. Step 2: internal canary on staging dedicated pool for 48h with traffic replay. Step 3: rollout to 5% of non-production tenants for 7 days. Step 4: gradual ramp to production critical tenants with SLA guardrails and abort-on-anomaly alerts. Rollback: disable flag and trigger controlled shrink to baseline autoscaler policy; notify affected tenants via ops runbook
telemetry_queries: # throttle_aware_scale_factor: custom metric emitted per decision: scale_factor = base_target * (1 - damping(throttle_rate))
experiments: A/B: baseline autoscaler vs throttle-aware autoscaler on identical replay traffic for 72h. Metrics: p95 latency, cost per QPS, capacity churn index
Sensitivity sweep: throttle_sensitivity in {0.1, 0.5, 1.0} and max_growth in {10, 20, 40} to find Pareto frontier
Tenant opt-out test: verify opt-out flag prevents policy from acting for selected tenants
risk_mitigation: Start canary on low-risk tenants and monitor churn and latency closely
Expose emergency kill-switch and automated rollback on >5% SLA regression
Add visibility: every scaling decision includes reason codes and metrics so oncall can triage quickly
Coordinate with rate-limiter and billing teams before enabling for enterprise customers
